summary: Preserved PR 3146's valid eager shared-prefix cascade decode implementation and added a CUDA-only regression that exercises the real FlashInfer paged-prefill wrappers and merge kernel against an independent PyTorch reference. The review counterexamples were reproduced. The implementation remains an explicitly partial integration: graph replay and unsupported attention/KV configurations still use ordinary decode, while actual FlashInfer execution and serving performance cannot be qualified on the prepared AMD ROCm node. The candidate's diff-hygiene defect is corrected in this consolidated patch.

tests.what_was_measured: Failing-before regression on the recorded base: 11 failures, 2 passes, 1 skip, with cascade helpers, metadata, updater, and forward path absent.

Passing-after regression: 6 tests and 7 subtests passed, covering selection boundaries, adversarial prefix mismatch, split page tables, scale propagation, merge dispatch, and an independent float64 GPU reference. The real FlashInfer integration test skipped because CUDA FlashInfer is unavailable.
Changed Python source and tests compile.
Consolidated correction has no whitespace errors; exact candidate 8f1eaa1 independently returned exit 2 with five trailing-whitespace findings.

gpu_execution_evidence: The portable float64 split-softmax comparison executed on one AMD Instinct MI355X through Torch 2.11.0+rocm7.2. No FlashInfer kernel executed: torch.version.cuda is null and importing flashinfer raises ModuleNotFoundError.
remaining_limitations: CUDA-graph decode continues to use ordinary decode wrappers; supporting dynamic shared-prefix eligibility requires a separately designed capture-stable graph path.
Sliding-window attention, encoder-decoder cross attention, speculative decode, and dequant-workspace KV cache configurations remain explicit non-cascade fallbacks.

The added real-wrapper numerical regression requires NVIDIA CUDA plus pinned FlashInfer 0.6.18 and skipped on this AMD ROCm node, so wrapper planning, cache layout, and kernel compatibility remain unverified here.
No NVIDIA end-to-end shared-prefix serving benchmark was possible. The tiny Llama fixture cannot exercise FlashInfer on this architecture and was not used as unrelated proof.
No native source changed, so no native rebuild was applicable.
